summary.text: Methane, CH₄, is a compound of one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms, the simplest alkane and the main part of natural gas.
In the atmosphere it lets visible light through but absorbs infrared radiation, so it acts as a greenhouse gas.
Methane forms through both geological and biological processes, and its largest store lies under the seafloor as methane clathrates.

facts.label: Beyond Earth
facts.value: Detected on other planets, including Mars

items.prompt: You notice a gas smell near a kitchen stove. Methane itself is odorless, so where does that smell come from?

options.label: Impurities picked up from underground rock
Methane reacting with oxygen in the room
Metal of the burner warming up
A smelly chemical added on purpose for safety

items.explain: Natural gas for homes gets its familiar smell from an added odorant, usually blends containing tert-butylthiol, as a safety measure.

items.prompt: Uranus and Neptune look blue or bluish-green from afar. What gives them that tint?

options.label: Methane in their air soaking up red light
Deep oceans of liquid water on their surfaces
Blue minerals in their rocky cores
Ice crystals bending sunlight like a prism

items.explain: Methane absorbs visible light, especially at the red end, over very long light paths; light passing through these methane-rich atmospheres is scattered back out bluish.

items.prompt: Methane is plentiful and makes an attractive fuel. What makes it hard to capture and store?

options.label: It explodes whenever it touches air
It is a gas at normal temperature and pressure
It eats through metal tanks
It breaks down within hours of collection

items.explain: Being a gas at standard temperature and pressure makes methane difficult to capture and store, despite its abundance.

items.prompt: One room's air holds 2% methane and a second room's holds 10%. A spark goes off in each. Where can the mixture burn?

options.label: Only in the 2% room
In both rooms
Only in the 10% room
In neither room

items.explain: Methane in air at standard pressure is flammable only between about 5.4% and 17%, so 2% is too lean while 10% falls inside the range.

items.prompt: A methane molecule has four identical carbon–hydrogen bonds spread evenly around the carbon. What shape does it take?

options.label: A flat square
A straight line
A flat triangle
A tetrahedron

items.explain: Methane is a tetrahedral molecule with four equivalent C–H bonds.

items.prompt: Visible light and infrared radiation both shine through air containing methane. How does methane behave?

options.label: It blocks visible light but passes infrared
It passes visible light but absorbs infrared
It absorbs both strongly, darkening the sky
It has no effect on either

items.explain: In Earth's atmosphere methane is transparent to visible light but absorbs infrared radiation, so it acts as a greenhouse gas.
